entries.03820015beec9cac: This business manufactures and sells automotive wire harnesses (bundles of wiring that carry electricity and signals within automobiles) and electrical components. External customer sales for the fiscal year ended March 2026 were ¥179,370 million, up 1.3% from ¥177,055 million in the fiscal year ended March 2025. The company explains that there were periods when it could not pass the effects of higher copper prices on to selling prices, while the reflection of one-time inflationary effects and other factors in selling prices progressed. Principal companies are the company itself and, in Japan, Fujikura Densō Co., Ltd.; overseas, Fujikura Automotive (Thailand) Ltd., Fujikura Automotive Vietnam Ltd., Zhuhai Fujikura Densō Co., Ltd., Fujikura Automotive Europe S.A.U., and others. Principal facilities include wire harness manufacturing facilities in Vietnam and Morocco.
entries.0afd080347640009: In its 2028 Medium-Term Management Plan, announced in May 2026, the company positions fiscal 2026 as the start of its “Fourth Founding.” Shifting from “defensive selection and concentration” to “offensive selection and concentration,” it will focus on three areas: “Information Infrastructure,” “Information Storage” and “Information Terminals.” It plans to allocate management resources with priority to “Information Infrastructure” and “Information Storage,” where demand from data centers is expected to expand. The company states that in March 2026 it decided to expand optical fiber cable production capacity to up to three times the current level. The company states that from fiscal 2026 the Electronics and Automotive Business Divisions will be integrated and operated as the Electronics and Electrical Components Business Division. It also states that it is pursuing initiatives in fusion energy, drawing on its technological capabilities.

entries.522d04b6e6296cd7: Profit attributable to owners of the parent for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥157,163 million, up 72.5% from ¥91,123 million in the previous fiscal year. Revenue rose 20.7% in the same year, and the company explains that growth in demand from data centers in Information and Communication, the largest division, pushed up revenue.
entries.54289ed1112060cb: This business manufactures and sells printed wiring boards, electronic wires, hard disk components and various connectors. External customer sales for the fiscal year ended March 2026 were ¥172,305 million, down 7.3% from ¥185,899 million in the fiscal year ended March 2025. The company explains that there were supply chain problems downstream, intensified competition, and higher costs due to a stronger Thai baht. Principal companies are the company itself and, in Japan, Tohoku Fujikura Co., Ltd. and Fujikura Purintosakitto Co., Ltd.; overseas, Fujikura Electronics (Thailand) Ltd., Fujikura Conec (THAILAND) LTD. and Fujikura Electronics (Shanghai) Co., Ltd., among others. Principal facilities include printed wiring board, electronic component and connector manufacturing facilities in Thailand, and a printed wiring board manufacturing facility in Akita City.

entries.6226c293d77f93a8: The group consists of Fujikura Ltd., 107 subsidiaries and 12 affiliates. It conducts manufacturing, sales and services of products across five business divisions: Information and Communication, Electronics, Automotive, Energy and Real Estate. Consolidated employees number 50,586 (as of March 31, 2026).
entries.6543d8381ab184f2: This business manufactures and sells optical fiber, optical cable, communication components, optical components, optical-related equipment and network equipment, and also performs construction work. External customer sales for the fiscal year ended March 2026 were ¥652,977 million, the largest among the five reportable segments and Other, up from ¥451,262 million in the fiscal year ended March 2025. The company explains that demand for data centers grew against the backdrop of the spread and expansion of generative AI, and that sales rose 44.7% year on year. Principal companies are the company itself and, in Japan, Fujikura Haioputo Co., Ltd. and Fujikura Solutions Ltd.; overseas, America Fujikura Ltd., AFL Telecommunications LLC and Fujikura Fenghuo Guangdian Cailiao Keji Co., Ltd., among others. Of these, AFL Telecommunications LLC of the United States had sales for the fiscal year ended March 2026 (excluding intra-group internal sales) of ¥355,383 million, accounting for more than 10% of consolidated net sales.

entries.f319dd6b01c538a0: In Information and Communication, it manufactures optical fibers, optical cables and optical components; in Electronics, printed wiring boards, electronic wires and connectors; in Automotive, automotive wire harnesses and electrical components; and in Energy, power cables and aluminum wires. For data centers, it has positioned the small-diameter, high-density optical fiber cable “SWR®/WTC®” as its strategic product.
entries.f5afefe80441387b: The company explains that its strategic product “SWR®/WTC®” is a source of competitiveness in the data center market: its small diameter and high density allow limited installation space to be used effectively and shorten connection time. It states that it has built a competitive edge by continuously launching new small-diameter, high-density cable products, and cites as its strengths a total solution for communication network installation, from optical fiber cables to fusion splicers, optical connectors, optical components and telecommunications engineering.
